items.note: Within-participants study in which design students ideate with an AI tool (SketchifAI) under text, sketch, or sketch-plus-tags prompting, with divergent-thinking performance (fluency, variety, originality, quality) scored; N and condition-order randomization not stated; arXiv 2606.26626 is the same work.

Quasi-experiment with 62 pre-service teachers comparing concept mapping plus generative AI (n = 30) with standalone generative AI (n = 32) on rated digital storytelling outcomes including innovation; AI-configuration comparison, not AI versus no AI.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page, web search); Semantic Scholar TLDR reports a pre/post creativity increase in an AI-intervention group of music students versus a comparison, so the creativity measure may be a test or self-report; search notes give N = 566 (unverified).

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect 403, web search); the title suggests a study of generative AI's effect on college students' creative problem solving, design unknown, so it goes to full text.

ECER 2025 conference abstract: 86 media art students randomly allocated to AI training plus generative tools (n = 29), AI training plus traditional digital tools (n = 28), or a control class (n = 29), all producing short-animation materials; unclear whether creativity is scored on the materials or measured as a creative-thinking test or mindset; conference abstract only, no full paper found.

Two empirical studies on how text, image, and 3D generative models support combinational design ideation; unclear whether human participants ideated under different AI configurations or whether only model outputs were compared, so it may be model-only.

Design case study comparing co-ideation with a custom GPT (Co-Ideator) against traditional ideation and a no-AI condition, with idea novelty and quality evaluated; abstract gives no N (search notes say 48) and no assignment details; also includes a separate designer survey.

Novice programmers using a CPS-structured ChatGPT assistant (CPS-GPT) versus a comparison condition, with gains in creativity (d = .557) and other outcomes; comparison condition, N, and whether creativity is scored on output or self-reported are not stated.

Within-subject study with 18 participants of Reflexa, an LLM reflection scaffold for creative coding, reporting improved originality and aesthetic quality; comparison condition not described and N is below 50.

Quasi-experiment with 120 music students in experimental (AI-assisted composition tools) and control groups, with compositions assessed pre and post on nine dimensions including creative fluency; check whether the tools are generative AI and whether the post-test was produced with AI available.
